notes: Clear hero, title, value prop and single primary CTA; strong first impression.
Page indicator: dot 3 is rendered lighter than the others with no explanation (skipped step?); reads as a rendering glitch.
Large empty band between feature list and footer; acceptable for onboarding.
Empty state is clear: icon, title, explanation, one primary 'Connect to barrier' action.
Content block floats mid-screen with ~200pt of dead space above it; anchor it higher (top third) like Apple Home empty states.
'Disconnected' chip is neutral grey; fine, but it duplicates the empty-state title.
State readable instantly: green tinted hero, flat arm, 'Lowered' + plain-language subtitle.
Header carries two lines of metrics (auth time, 'Phone-measured, simulated. Reference: 2.00 s') above the chips; dense for an end user, pushes the hero down.
Footnote 'An accepted command starts a monitored movement...' is engineering copy on the main control screen.
Disabled Lower uses the neutral style and the hint 'Already lowered.' explains why; good.
STOP at rest is tinted (not filled) while Raise is filled; hierarchy is correct.
Best state on the screen: angled arm, blue 'Raising', progress '0.8 s of about 4.0 s', filled red STOP, both directions disabled with 'Arm is moving. Use Stop.'
Progress bar is thin (about 4pt) and short; a touch more weight would help at arm's length.
Raised state reads clearly (blue hero, vertical arm).
Success toast 'Barrier is up' is green while the Raised state color is blue; two semantic colors for one event. Acceptable per tokens (success = completed) but slightly noisy.
Toast + hint 'Already raised.' + disabled Raise say the same thing three times.
Amber hero with mid-angle arm and 'Raise or lower to continue' is clear and actionable.
Toast 'Stopped for safety' duplicates the hero and gives no cause while all chips are green; if the user pressed STOP, say 'Stopped' (or name the cause).
No hint line above the buttons here, unlike every other state; the button block shifts up.
Warning banner 'Can't move right now' with cause and remedy is well written.
Raise remains the filled primary button directly under a banner saying motion was refused; mixed signal. Demote it (tinted) while zone is blocked, or keep enabled but add 'Try again' wording.
Hero stays green 'Lowered' with no hint of the block; only the amber 'Zone blocked' chip and banner carry it.
No visible entry to the Safety checks sheet from the banner (add 'Details' / chevron).
Fault is unmistakable: red hero, warning glyph, 'Needs on-site reset' card with the exact recovery step and 'The app cannot clear a fault.'
Hero card collapses to about 70% of the height used by every other state and the arm/base illustration is drawn at a smaller scale; the whole screen jumps when entering FAULT.
Hero shows only the cause ('Position sensors disagree') with no state word; 'Fault' never appears as the state label.
'Sensors: see fault' chip is neutral grey instead of danger; weakest signal for the failing item.
STOP stays tinted/enabled while 'Controls locked.'; fine if intentional (STOP always reachable) but the hint should say 'Lower and Raise locked'.
Neutral hero, dashed ghost arm, '?' glyph and 'Lower it to home the barrier' make the required action obvious; Lower is the only filled button.
The '?' glyph floats alone at the top of the hero; slightly disconnected from the title.
Connection-lost banner with inline Reconnect, 'Last known: Raising / Not live', clock-badged stale chips and disabled controls: very good offline treatment.
Hero illustration is drawn at a smaller scale than the live states (base narrower, arm shorter); visible size jump.
Header loses the auth subtitle and chips move up; layout shifts between connected and lost states.
Light: the dimmed arm renders as isolated pink stripes with the white segments invisible against the white card; it looks broken, not 'stale'. Use a grey outline or reduced-opacity full arm.
Clean modal: large title, section header, single inset row with 'Previously paired' pill, signal bars, chevron.
No scanning indicator or 'last scanned' time; 'Scan again' is the only clue a scan happened.
'Close' text button sits ~40pt below the top edge with nothing beside it; consider a grabber or standard sheet header.
Grouped inset sections (Barrier, Safety interlocks, Power) feel native; big 12.90 V readout with 'Healthy' pill.
Circular cloud-slash button next to the 'Connected' chip has no label; meaning (local only?) is not obvious and it looks tappable.
State 'Raised' is plain grey value text with no state color/icon, unlike the rest of the app.
Movement guard row is a long paragraph inside a value list; better as footer text.
Good empty state with Connect CTA.
Requirement codes (C4, C5, S5, S6) and 'Nothing here is a verdict' are project-review language on an end-user tab; move to Presenter or About.
Full-width filled 'Share CSV' is the most prominent element on the screen; export is secondary. Use a share icon in the header (or a plain/tinted button below the summary).
Every row carries a status pill that repeats the row title ('State Stopped' + 'Stopped'); rows are ~100pt tall and only 5 fit. Fold status into the icon/title color and drop the pill.
Command rows and state rows interleave with identical weight; consider grouping state changes under their command.
Segmented filter and Evidence summary disclosure are good.
Textbook grouped settings: section headers, segmented controls, icon rows with chevrons, toggle.
Segmented controls are wrapped in their own white card; a plain segmented control on the grouped background (or in a row) is more native.
Locked 'Bluetooth' segment is explained by the footer; good.
Scenario cards with title, description, step-count and FSM chips are scannable; SIMULATED badge always visible.
Bottom 'Exit presenter' bar cuts the next card mid-word; fine as scroll content but a fade/blur would look more finished.
Two choice cards with selected state (blue border, tint, checkmark) are clear.
Unavailable 'I have the barrier here' card still looks like a selectable white card; dim the whole card (title/icon) more strongly.
Clear permission primer with primary 'Allow Bluetooth' and 'Not now'.
Large empty middle; a short 'what happens next' line or illustration would balance it.
Numbered step cards with trailing icons communicate the flow; 'Connect becomes available once the timer is running' explains the disabled path.

Timer ring: the '1:00' numerals are wider than the ring's inner diameter and overlap the ring stroke; 'not started' also crosses the stroke at the bottom. Visible overlap on the screen's focal element.
Footnote 'A barrier can have up to 2 owner phones.' sits directly on the footer divider (clipped/colliding); content needs bottom padding or must scroll above the footer.
Step 1 copy runs four lines in bold; shorten (e.g. 'Tap Start to open the 60 s pairing window.').
Clear completion with single CTA.
Design intent calls for 'You're the owner' + 'Authenticated in X.XX s'; simulator copy is fine but the screen is mostly empty.
Native detail list with footers and a separate destructive 'Forget this barrier' row.
'Barrier's last counter 0' while Health shows 1 in the same capture set; make sure both read the same source or label one 'last reported'.
Polished: app icon, name, team line, version rows, privacy and scope notes.
No licenses row (listed in DESIGN 3.4).
Checklist with icon + label + status, failing item expanded with cause, remedy and 'Blocked your last command'; excellent.
Secondary lines often restate the title ('Sensors valid / Valid', 'No fault latched / No fault').
Sheet header uses a medium title rather than the app's large-title pattern; acceptable for a sheet.
Step list (Connected / Securing / Checking owner / Ready) with spinner on the active step makes progress clear.
Subtitle 'Securing (pairing)...' repeats the active step label.
Passkey help card is useful; the mock Android dialog is low-contrast grey on tint (decorative, acceptable).
No explicit Cancel for the in-flight pairing besides 'Close'.
Hero + step pager + step card + live state table is a good projector layout.
State table has three columns with no headers ('State | Raised | Raised', 'Fault | No fault | None'); the duplicated right column is unexplained. Add 'Shown / Raw' headers or drop one.
Step 1 says 'LOWER: The arm starts down from RAISED' while hero shows idle Raised and status 'Ready'; fine, but label the action as pending ('Next: LOWER').
Step card with 'As expected', expectations checklist and REJECTED_GUARD / 0x10 secondary codes works well for the demo.
Current step circle combines blue ring with green 'done' fill; ambiguous whether it passed or is current.
Red fault hero with dashed arm and step evidence is clear.
Fault hero again shorter than other heroes (no subtitle line).
Clear step narrative; codes shown as secondary text as intended.
Step description is 4 lines of 17pt grey text; slightly heavy for a projector, consider a shorter lead plus the checklist.
Capture starts mid-scroll (top card cut off, title not visible); first viewport could not be judged.
Stepper label 'Simulated median (next run)' wraps with an orphaned 'run)' between the -100/+100 buttons; shorten to 'Next-run median'.
Histogram with 2.0 s spec line, stats row and 'Phone-measured, simulated' caption is good.
Same headerless three-column state table ('Lowered | Lowered'); 'Guard: No block' value is dimmer than its siblings.
